summary: A seasonal guide to foraging and cooking wild mushrooms through autumn 2023, structured around the author's outings with a forager, a mycologist, an environmentalist, a chef and a preserver. It covers when species appear, essential gear, safe identification, sustainable harvesting, cooking, preserving and the community around foraging. It closes by stressing respect for ecosystems and the lessons of the season.
one_line: An autumn 2023 guide to foraging, identifying, ethically harvesting, cooking and preserving wild mushrooms, told through expert-led outings and community events.
key_facts: The foraging season described began around September 15, 2023, with enthusiasts gearing up with baskets and field guides.
Emily Henderson of Forest Bounty Forays says oyster mushrooms can be spotted beside aspen trunks as early as September.
Porcini and chanterelles emerge in October in dappled woodlands, while November rains bring out the elusive matsutake.
The recommended forager's toolkit includes a woven basket, a small knife for cutting stems, a soft brush, a field guide, and a compass or GPS device.
On October 12, mycologist Dr. Samuel Richards held an identification workshop in Deepwoods National Park, warning "Never eat anything unless you're 100% sure of its identity."
Key identifiers for mushrooms are cap shape, color, gill attachment, stem characteristics, spore print color, and the growing environment; the mantra is "when in doubt, throw it out."
On October 29, environmentalist Laura Kim led a sustainability-focused forage, stressing taking only what is needed and not disturbing the mycelium.
On November 5th in an old oak grove, the author found hen of the woods and a lone morel with a honeycomb cap.
On November 14th, chef Marco Giovanni sautéed chanterelles in butter with garlic and served porcini in creamy risotto, advising "The key is simplicity."
On December 3rd, Anne Smith demonstrated preservation: chanterelles sliced and dried on racks, and oyster mushrooms pickled in a brine of vinegar and spices.
On December 12th, a local foraging group shared experiences and dishes at the annual Fungi Fest.
The author concludes that the season taught environmental stewardship as well as cooking and identification.
